literal: Zhangsun Song, Zhangsun Daosheng, Zhangsun Fei
idiomatic: Volume 22 Biographies 10: Zhangsun Song, Zhangsun Daosheng, Zhangsun Fei

literal: Biographies 10
idiomatic: Biographies 10

literal: Zhangsun Song
idiomatic: Zhangsun Song

literal: Zhangsun Song was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Zhangsun Song came from Dai.

literal: His father Ren, in Zhaocheng's time, was Southern Tribal Elder.
idiomatic: His father Ren served as Southern Tribal Elder under Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: Song was broad-minded and elegant, with capacity and measure; Zhaocheng bestowed the name upon him.
idiomatic: Song was magnanimous and dignified; Zhaocheng gave him the name Song.

literal: At fourteen he succeeded his father in leading affairs.
idiomatic: At fourteen he took his father's place in command.

literal: In Zhaocheng's last years the tribes fell into disorder; Fu Jian sent Liu Kuren to take charge of state affairs, and Song with Yuan Ta and others led their followers to submit to him.
idiomatic: Late in Zhaocheng's reign the tribes were in turmoil; Fu Jian sent Liu Kuren to govern the realm, and Song with Yuan Ta and others brought their people to join him.

literal: When Liu Xian plotted treachery, Song led his old followers and the Shushi clan—more than seven hundred households—to rebel against Xian and flee.
idiomatic: When Liu Xian turned traitor, Song led his veterans and the Shushi, over seven hundred households, to break with Xian and escape.

literal: As he was about to reach Wuyuan, Shijun's son Wo had also gathered a following and set himself up; Song wished to join him.
idiomatic: Near Wuyuan, Prince Shi's son Wo had raised troops and declared himself leader; Song meant to go to him.

literal: Meeting Wu Wo, he called Wo a son who had turned against his father and urged Song to return to Daowu.
idiomatic: He met Wu Wo, who denounced Wo as a rebel against his father and urged Song to submit to Daowu.

literal: Song had not yet decided; Wu Wo turned his ox's head back, and Song bowed low and followed, meeting Daowu at Erhan Pavilion.
idiomatic: Song hesitated; Wu Wo turned his ox homeward, and Song bowed and went along, meeting Daowu at Erhan Pavilion.

literal: Daowu made him Southern Tribal Elder; he repeatedly distinguished himself in military service.
idiomatic: Daowu appointed him Southern Tribal Elder, and he won repeated distinction in the field.

literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan, was made Governor of Ji Province, and enfeoffed Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: He later joined the attack on Zhongshan, was made Governor of Ji Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.

literal: He served in turn as Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiang Province, and was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping.
idiomatic: In succession he was Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiang Province, and was raised to Duke of Nanping.

literal: Wherever he served he won renown.
idiomatic: In every post he earned praise.

literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, the Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin, the Marquis of Beixin An Tong, the Marquis of Baima Cui Hong, and five others sat to the right of the imperial carriage gate and heard state affairs—hence the age called them the Eight Dukes.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan succeeded, Xi Jin of Shanyang, An Tong of Beixin, Cui Hong of Baima, and five others sat at the right of the Stop-the-Carriage Gate and governed affairs; the age called them the Eight Dukes.

literal: When the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Mingyuan lent Song his staff of authority to supervise military affairs east of the mountains; he went to Pingyuan and drew up his army along the north bank of the Yellow River, encamping at Pancheng.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu of Jin marched against Yao Hong, Mingyuan gave Song command authority over the eastern armies; he reached Pingyuan and lined his forces along the north bank of the Yellow River, camping at Pancheng.

literal: The army suffered some setbacks.
idiomatic: The campaign met reverses.

literal: An edict granted Liu Yu passage.
idiomatic: The court issued an edict granting Liu Yu free passage.

literal: From his boat Liu Yu saw Song's banners and canopies and sent him wine from Ling and foods of the south.
idiomatic: Liu Yu, aboard ship, sighted Song's standards and sent Ling wine and southern delicacies.

literal: Song sent them all to the capital.
idiomatic: Song forwarded everything to the capital.

literal: An edict ordered Song to respond generously.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered Song to reply in kind.

literal: He also commanded that picked troops be readied for war; if Yu passed westward, Song was to lead elite forces south through Peng and Pei;
idiomatic: He further ordered elite troops held in readiness: if Yu marched west, Song was to drive crack units south through Peng and Pei;

literal: if he did not pass in good time, he was only to follow with his army.
idiomatic: if Yu did not pass promptly, he was merely to trail him with his army.

literal: When Yu reached the region between Xiao and Shan, he would surely be locked with Yao Hong; one would die and one be wounded, and their forces would be worn out.
idiomatic: When Yu reached the ground between Xiao and Shan he would surely grapple with Yao Hong; one side would perish and one be crippled, and both armies exhausted.

literal: By autumn one could strike at leisure, and Liu Yu's head could be hung without a battle.
idiomatic: Come autumn one could strike at ease, and Liu Yu's head might be taken without fighting.

literal: Thereupon Sunsun Jian and others [were dispatched].
idiomatic: Thereupon Sunsun Jian and others were sent.

literal: They followed the river toward Luo and entered the passes.
idiomatic: They advanced along the river toward Luoyang and entered the passes.

literal: Song and Jian and the rest crossed south from Chenggao; Jin garrisons everywhere fled at the dust of their approach.
idiomatic: Song and Jian crossed south from Chenggao; Jin border posts broke and ran at their dust.

literal: When Yu took Chang'an, Song withdrew his army.
idiomatic: After Yu seized Chang'an, Song marched home.

literal: Mingyuan, lying ill, asked Song about affairs after his death.
idiomatic: Mingyuan, on his sickbed, asked Song about the succession.

literal: Song said, "To install the eldest is accord with order; to install by virtue is to win men's hearts.
idiomatic: Song said, "To set up the eldest son is to follow order; to choose by virtue is to win obedience.

literal: Now the eldest imperial son is worthy and the legitimate heir—the mandate of Heaven; I ask that he be enthroned.
idiomatic: The eldest imperial son is worthy and the rightful heir; Heaven has chosen him. I beg that he be enthroned.

literal: " The policy was settled; an edict had Taiwu attend court and oversee the state, with Song as left assistant.
idiomatic: " The decision was made; Taiwu was ordered to preside at court and oversee the realm, with Song as his left-hand counselor.

literal: When Taiwu took the throne, Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping and Director of the Right for Si Province.
idiomatic: When Taiwu succeeded, Song was raised to Prince of Beiping and made Director of the Right for Si Province.

literal: An edict asked the ministers, "Helian and Rouran—which should we campaign against first?
idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, "Helian and Rouran—which should we attack first?

literal: " Song with the Prince of Pingyang Zhangsun Han and the Minister of Works Xi Jin said, "Helian holds fixed territory and cannot yet be a grave threat.
idiomatic: " Song, the Prince of Pingyang Zhangsun Han, and Minister of Works Xi Jin said, "Helian sits on settled ground and is not yet a great danger.

literal: Rouran has for generations been a border scourge; we should first strike Datan.
idiomatic: Rouran has long plagued the frontier; Datan should be attacked first.

literal: If we catch him in time we can seize his herds and flocks and enrich the state;
idiomatic: If we catch him in time we can take his herds and enrich the treasury;

literal: if not, we can hunt on Yin Mountain, kill many beasts, and fill our stores with meat, hide, sinew, and horn—still better than crushing a petty state.
idiomatic: if not, we can hunt Yin Mountain, slaughter game, and stock the army with meat, hides, sinew, and horn—better still than wasting force on a small realm.

literal: " The Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao said, "Datan shifts like birds in flight; swift pursuit cannot be sustained long, and a great host cannot overtake him.
idiomatic: " Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao said, "Datan moves like a fleeing bird; hot pursuit cannot last, and a mass army cannot catch him.

literal: Helian Qubugai's domain is less than a thousand li; his punishments and government are cruel—the people and spirits have cast him off; he should be attacked first.
idiomatic: Helian Qubugai holds less than a thousand li; his laws are savage and men and gods have abandoned him—strike him first.

literal: " The Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie and the Marquis of Wujing An Yuan asked that Feng Ba be pacified first.
idiomatic: " Director Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing An Yuan urged pacifying Feng Ba first.

literal: The emperor was silent and then made a western tour of inspection.
idiomatic: The emperor said nothing and went west on inspection.

literal: Later, hearing Qubugai had died and Guanzhong was in great disorder, they debated marching against it.
idiomatic: Later, when word came that Qubugai was dead and Guanzhong in chaos, the court debated a western campaign.

literal: Song and others said, "If they hold their cities and wait at ease for our weariness,
idiomatic: Song and others said, "If they shut their walls and wait while we tire ourselves,

literal: when Datan hears of it he will raid in our absence—a perilous road.
idiomatic: Datan will hear and strike our emptiness—that road is perilous.

literal: " The emperor then questioned the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi of Youzheng.
idiomatic: " The emperor then consulted the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi.

literal: Qianzhi urged the march; Du Chao seconded it; Cui Hao again argued that a western campaign would profit.
idiomatic: Qianzhi urged action; Du Chao agreed; Cui Hao again pressed the gains of a western war.

literal: Song and others firmly remonstrated that it could not be done; the emperor was furious, accused Song of corruption in office, and had warriors publicly humiliate him.
idiomatic: Song and others protested that it must not be done; the emperor raged, charged Song with corruption, and had guards shame him before the court.

literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Commandant.

literal: After a long while he was additionally made Pillar of State and Grand General.
idiomatic: In time he was also made Pillar of State and Grand General.

literal: From then on, whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign,
idiomatic: After that, whenever the emperor marched out,

literal: Song as an elder statesman mostly remained to guard the capital, sitting in court to judge criminal cases.
idiomatic: Song as a senior pillar mostly stayed to guard the capital, presiding in court to decide criminal suits.

literal: He died at eighty; his posthumous name was Xuan.
idiomatic: He died at eighty; his posthumous name was Xuan.

literal: Later Xiaowen recorded the merits of earlier reigns and had Song given joint sacrifice in the ancestral hall.
idiomatic: Later Xiaowen honored founders of earlier reigns and granted Song joint offerings in the imperial temple.

literal: His son Tui was skilled at mounted archery and could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
idiomatic: His son Tui excelled in horsemanship and archery and could bend a three-hundred-jin bow.

literal: He inherited the title and was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: He inherited the rank and was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.

literal: For an offense he was demoted to a border soldier.
idiomatic: For a crime he was reduced to garrison duty.

literal: Later his title was restored.
idiomatic: His title was later restored.

literal: He died; his posthumous name was An.
idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was An.

literal: His son Dun, style name Xiaoyou, was Northern Garrison Commander-in-Chief.
idiomatic: His son Dun, styled Xiaoyou, became Northern Garrison Commander-in-Chief.

literal: For venality he was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: For corruption he was demoted from prince to duke.

literal: In Xiaowen's time he pleaded that his forebears' merit was weighty and had his princely rank restored.
idiomatic: Under Xiaowen he argued that his ancestors' service was great and recovered his princely title.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His posthumous name was Jian.
idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jian.

literal: His son Dao, style name Nianseng, inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Dao, styled Nianseng, succeeded to the title.

literal: After a long while, following the usual rule, he was reduced to duke and made Left Guards General.
idiomatic: In time, by the usual rule, he was demoted to duke and made Left Guards General.

literal: He died; his posthumous name was Shen.
idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Shen.

literal: His son Yue inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Yue inherited the title.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he recovered his original princely rank; soon he was again reduced to duke and made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: At the opening of Jianyi he regained his princely rank; soon he was again demoted to duke and made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

literal: He died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

literal: Fifth-generation descendant Jian
idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant Jian

literal: Song's fifth-generation descendant Jian became renowned in Zhou service.
idiomatic: Song's fifth-generation descendant Jian won fame serving the Zhou.

literal: Jian's original name was Qingming.
idiomatic: Jian had originally been named Qingming.

literal: His great-grandfather Difen was General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Linchuan.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Difen was General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Linchuan.

literal: His grandfather Zhuo was Governor of Heng Province.
idiomatic: His grandfather Zhuo was Governor of Heng Province.

literal: His father Yi was Outer Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library and died young.
idiomatic: His father Yi was Outer Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library and died young.

literal: Jian was square and upright in conduct, stern in bearing; even in private quarters he remained grave all day.
idiomatic: Jian was upright and principled, grave in manner; even at home he sat in formal bearing all day.

literal: He would not associate lightly; unless they were kindred in spirit, even noble visitors at his gate he would not receive.
idiomatic: He made no casual friendships; unless they shared his principles, even grandees at his door went unseen.

literal: In Taichang, when the frontier was disturbed, Jian was first made Acting Grand Commander for Defense of East Xia Province; following Erzhu Tianhe he defeated Su Qin Mingda and others and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Suolu.
idiomatic: In the Taichang era, when the border stirred, Jian was first Acting Grand Commander for Defense of East Xia Province; he followed Erzhu Tianhe in defeating Su Qin Mingda and was enfeoffed Marquis of Suolu.

literal: When Zhou Wen came to Xia Province he made Jian Recording Secretary and greatly respected and valued him.
idiomatic: When Zhou Wen arrived at Xia Province he made Jian Recording Secretary and held him in high regard.

literal: When Heba Yue was killed, Zhou Wen went to Pingliang; whenever there was strategy for governing the realm, Jian took part.
idiomatic: After Heba Yue was slain, Zhou Wen went to Pingliang; on every plan for rule Jian was consulted.

literal: Following the pacification of Hou Mo Chen Yue, Jian was left as Chief Administrator of Qin Province and Grand Commander for Defense, entrusted with affairs behind the lines, and additionally enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.
idiomatic: After Hou Mo Chen Yue was pacified, Jian was left Chief Administrator of Qin and Grand Commander for Defense, entrusted with the rear, and enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.

literal: After Governor of Wei Province Kezhu Hunyuan fled to Eastern Wei, hearts between the Yellow and Wei rivers were divided.
idiomatic: When Wei Governor Kezhu Hunyuan fled to Eastern Wei, loyalty between the Yellow and Wei rivers frayed.

literal: Governor Li Bi had Jian act as temporary commander of Wei Province.
idiomatic: Governor Li Bi put Jian in temporary charge of Wei Province.

literal: Jian took a dozen horsemen and braved hardship to go there.
idiomatic: Jian rode out with a dozen men through danger to reach it.

literal: He then soothed according to circumstances; Qiang and Hu submitted gladly.
idiomatic: He then pacified as the moment required; Qiang and Hu submitted willingly.

literal: He was transferred to Governor of Xia Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Xia Province.

literal: He won great harmony among the people.
idiomatic: He won deep goodwill among the people.

literal: At that time Western Xia Province had still not submitted within the realm, while Eastern Wei sent Xu He as governor.
idiomatic: Western Xia Province had not yet joined the realm; Eastern Wei sent Xu He as its governor.

literal: Jian won him by faith and righteousness; He then submitted.
idiomatic: Jian won him with faith and duty; He then came over.

literal: Jian was at once made Governor of Western Xia and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for the three Xia provinces.
idiomatic: He was immediately made Governor of Western Xia and supreme commander of the three Xia provinces.

literal: When Jing and Xiang first submitted, Zhou Wen memorialized to appoint Jian Commander-in-Chief of twelve provinces including the three Jings, Governor of Jing, and Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit.
idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang first submitted, Zhou Wen memorialized making Jian commander of twelve provinces including the three Jings, Governor of Jing, and Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit.

literal: Magistrate Quan Can of Zheng County in his jurisdiction was sued by the people; investigation proved the charges true.
idiomatic: The magistrate of Zheng County, Quan Can, was accused by the people and investigation proved him guilty.

literal: Jian at once gathered his staff, then before the investigation hall cited his own fault, bared his torso and punished himself, and let Can go without inquiry.
idiomatic: Jian immediately assembled his staff, confessed his own fault before the investigation hall, stripped and flogged himself, and released Can without punishment.

literal: Thereafter subordinate cities were stirred to discipline and none dared break the law.
idiomatic: Subordinate districts were awed into order and none dared offend the law.

literal: Emperor Wen of Wei sent an imperial letter commending him.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei sent a sealed letter of praise.

literal: Zhou Wen also wrote to Jian, saying, "Recently I heard that a magistrate in your jurisdiction had committed an offense, and you yourself administered thirty strokes to discipline your subordinates; on hearing it I rejoiced and sighed for a long time, beyond words.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen also wrote to Jian: "I have just heard that a magistrate under you offended, and you yourself took thirty strokes to awe your staff. I rejoiced and sighed a long while at the news—words fail me.
